finding.claim: Broken access control on DELETE /projects/:id. The handler calls `authorized(req.user, project)`, which returns a boolean instead of throwing, and discards the result. The throwing helper `authorize` is used in the PUT handler, but not here. Any authenticated user can delete any other user's project.
finding.source: Authenticated non-owner, non-admin user sends DELETE /projects/<victim project id>. The :id path parameter is attacker-controlled.

trace.note: DELETE /projects/:id handler receives the attacker-supplied id
Project is looked up by id only, with no ownership filter
authorized() returns false for a non-owner, but the return value is ignored, so execution continues
authorized() only returns a boolean and never throws (unlike authorize at line 4)

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the authorized() call at line 18, and it is a no-op because its result is unused. No router-level middleware or other ownership check exists in this file. req.user is populated elsewhere, outside this repo, so authentication of the caller is assumed. The PUT /projects/:id/name handler correctly uses the throwing authorize(), which shows the intended control.

verdict.guard_found: Only authorized() at api.js:18, which returns a boolean (api.js:12-14) and whose result is discarded. No router-level middleware or other ownership check exists in the directory.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls the boolean-returning authorized() (defined at api.js:12-14) as a bare statement, so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated non-owner, unlike the throwing authorize() used at api.js:25.
